title: Five Indians Arrested in Thailand for Kidnapping Three Indian Tourists in Pattaya
excerpt: The victims were lured with a fake tour package, held captive for days, and subjected to staged torture as their captors demanded ransom — all allegedly directed by a Dubai-based Pakistani national.
body:
• Thai police arrested five Indian nationals in Bangkok on Tuesday for kidnapping three Indian tourists in Pattaya, holding them captive for days, and demanding ₹40 lakh ($47,000) in ransom from each victim's family.
  • The victims — aged 20 to 24 — were lured to Thailand with a fake seven-day tour package, then confined, bound, beaten, and hung upside down by their captors.
  • Police say the suspects were directed by a Pakistani national based in Dubai, who planned to receive ransom payments in cryptocurrency.
  • The three victims were rescued from a Pattaya property on Monday after a relative alerted the Indian Embassy, which coordinated with Thai authorities.

Lured by a Fake Tour Package

Thai police have arrested five Indian nationals for kidnapping and torturing three young Indian tourists in the resort city of Pattaya, in a case that has exposed a cross-border criminal operation allegedly directed from Dubai.

https://x.com/NewsX/status/2082518262483661065

The three victims — identified as Mohit, 23, Ashish, 24, and Himanshu, 20 — arrived at Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport on July 21 after booking what they believed was a legitimate seven-day Pattaya tour package worth approximately ₹1.99 lakh (70,000 Thai baht). Upon reaching Pattaya, they were approached by an Indian man who transported them individually by motorcycle to a residential property, where they were held captive.

Days of Captivity and Staged Torture

According to Thai police, the victims were confined in two bedrooms with their limbs and mouths bound. Over several days, they were beaten, kept without food, and hung upside down. In one particularly calculated act of cruelty, the captors sprayed red paint on the victims' bodies to simulate bleeding injuries during video calls with their families in India.

The kidnappers demanded ransom payments of ₹40 lakh (approximately $47,000) per victim, using the staged footage to pressure families into paying. A relative of one victim eventually contacted the Indian Embassy in Bangkok, which alerted Thai immigration officials and Pattaya police on July 21.

"Officers rescued the three victims on Monday, finding them locked in two bedrooms with their limbs and mouths bound. The suspects fled the property on motorcycles just minutes before police arrived."

— Thai police statement

Arrests in a Bangkok Hotel

Police traced the suspects through phone numbers used during ransom negotiations, one of which was registered in Dubai. Investigators tracked five Indian nationals — Avtar Singh, 38, Jagjit Singh, 38, Rambalak Kumar, 24, Sukhbir Singh, 37, and Kulra Singh, 27 — to a hotel in Bangkok's Khlong Tan area.

Officers arrested all five in the hotel lobby and upstairs rooms on Tuesday, just hours before they were scheduled to board flights out of Thailand. The suspects told police they had been recruited and directed by a Pakistani national through an encrypted messaging application for approximately one month.

A Dubai-Based Operation

Thai investigators believe the mastermind behind the kidnapping is based in Dubai and had planned to receive ransom payments in cryptocurrency, making them harder to trace. The suspects said they had been promised cash, valuables, and airline tickets out of Thailand once the operation was complete.

The case echoes a broader pattern of South Asian nationals being targeted in transnational kidnapping-for-ransom schemes across Southeast Asia, where lighter regulatory environments and large diaspora populations create opportunities for criminal networks. Thailand, in particular, has seen a rise in crimes involving foreign nationals, with authorities arresting approximately 700 foreign nationals this year in connection with various fraud and criminal operations.

What's Next

All five suspects are in Thai police custody and face charges of kidnapping, unlawful detention, and extortion. Thai authorities are working with Indian and Emirati counterparts to identify and locate the alleged Dubai-based mastermind.

The Indian Embassy has assisted the three victims, who are recovering from their ordeal. The case has prompted calls from Indian travelers' associations for stricter vetting of overseas tour packages and greater consular vigilance in popular tourist destinations across Southeast Asia.
nri_angle: Indian tourists increasingly targeted in Southeast Asian kidnapping schemes; raises consular protection concerns for the growing Indian traveler population in Thailand.
